survey: Front-facing anchor, slightly rotated clockwise. Ring at the top of the shank, facing the camera as a near-circle. Stock (crossbar) passes through a collar below the ring; its left ball end is slightly larger than the right, so the bar recedes gently to the right, which fits a mild three-quarter turn. The shank is a cylinder leaning top-right. A rope runs through the ring and spirals down the shank in shallow tilted ellipses that pass in front of and behind the cylinder. The arms and flukes meet at the crown, at right angles to the shank; the right arm sits lower, which matches the clockwise lean. There is no ground: the anchor floats on a flat striped background, so there is no contact to check. Shank tilt, crossbar foreshortening, arm angle and ring orientation all agree on one viewpoint.
